import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Yau's conjecture on the first eigenvalue

Yau's conjecture (1982) states that the first (nonzero) eigenvalue of the Laplace–Beltrami
operator on a closed embedded minimal hypersurface $M^n$ of the unit sphere $S^{n+1}$ is $n$.

Mathlib does not (yet) have the Laplace–Beltrami operator or the mean curvature of a Riemannian
submanifold. Since the hypersurfaces in question are submanifolds of the Euclidean space
$\mathbb{R}^{n+2}$, we define these notions extrinsically, from the ambient calculus:

* the tangent space of $M$ at $\iota(x)$ is the image of the differential of the embedding $\iota$;
* the gradient of a function on $M$ is the tangential projection of the ambient gradient, i.e.
  the unique tangent vector representing the differential of the function on the tangent space;
* the divergence of a tangent vector field $X$ along $M$ is the trace over the tangent space of
  $v \mapsto P(D_v X)$, where $P$ is the orthogonal projection onto the tangent space and
  $D_v X$ is the ambient derivative of $X$ along $M$ in the tangent direction $v$; this is the
  trace of the Levi-Civita covariant derivative of the induced metric;
* the Laplace–Beltrami operator is $\Delta f = \operatorname{div}(\nabla f)$;
* the mean curvature vector of $M$ in $\mathbb{R}^{n+2}$ is $\vec H = \Delta \iota$, the Laplacian
  of the position vector (equivalently, the trace of the second fundamental form);
* $M \subseteq S^{n+1}$ is minimal in $S^{n+1}$ if its mean curvature vector in $S^{n+1}$, which is
  the component of $\vec H$ tangent to the sphere, vanishes, i.e. $\vec H(p)$ is a multiple of $p$.

Derivatives along $M$ are taken with `fderivWithin` on the image of $\iota$; on tangent vectors
these are uniquely determined, and the definitions above depend only on their values on tangent
vectors.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Yau's conjecture on the first eigenvalue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yau%27s_conjecture_on_the_first_eigenvalue)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- S.-T. Yau, *Seminar on Differential Geometry*, Annals of Mathematics Studies 102, Princeton
  University Press, 1982, Problem Section.
- Z. Tang, W. Yan, *Isoparametric foliation and Yau conjecture on the first eigenvalue*,
  J. Differential Geom. 94 (2013), 521–540, [arXiv:1201.0666](https://arxiv.org/abs/1201.0666).
-/
open scoped Manifold ContDiff
open Manifold
namespace YausConjectureOnTheFirstEigenvalue

blocks.command_arg: {n : ℕ} {M : Type*} [TopologicalSpace M] [ChartedSpace (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) M]
blocks.text:
variable {n : ℕ} {M : Type*} [TopologicalSpace M] [ChartedSpace (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) M]
  (ι : M → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (n + 2)))

blocks.code:
noncomputable def ambientTangentSpace (x : M) : Submodule ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (n + 2))) :=
  LinearMap.range (mfderiv (𝓡 n) 𝓘(ℝ, EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (n + 2))) ι x).toLinearMap
blocks.docstring:
The tangent space at `ι x` of the submanifold `Set.range ι` of `ℝ^{n+2}`, as a subspace of
the ambient Euclidean space: the image of the differential of `ι` at `x`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Mathlib `TangentSpace` (abstract model-space copy, not a subspace of the ambient space) and `tangentConeAt` (equal for embedded submanifolds but less transparent).
justification.name: YausConjectureOnTheFirstEigenvalue.ambientTangentSpace
justification.why_needed: Tangent space of the embedded submanifold at ι x as a subspace of the ambient Euclidean space (range of mfderiv ι x), needed to project and take traces extrinsically.

blocks.name: ambientTangentSpace
blocks.text:
/-- The tangent space at `ι x` of the submanifold `Set.range ι` of `ℝ^{n+2}`, as a subspace of
the ambient Euclidean space: the image of the differential of `ι` at `x`. -/
noncomputable def ambientTangentSpace (x : M) : Submodule ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (n + 2))) :=
  LinearMap.range (mfderiv (𝓡 n) 𝓘(ℝ, EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (n + 2))) ι x).toLinearMap

blocks.code:
noncomputable def tangentialGradient (f : M → ℝ) (x : M) : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (n + 2)) :=
  (ambientTangentSpace ι x).starProjection
    ((InnerProductSpace.toDual ℝ _).symm
      (fderivWithin ℝ (Function.extend ι f 0) (Set.range ι) (ι x)))
blocks.docstring:
The gradient at `ι x` of a function `f : M → ℝ` with respect to the metric induced by `ι`,
as a vector of the ambient space. It is the orthogonal projection onto the tangent space of the
ambient gradient of `f ∘ ι⁻¹` along `Set.range ι`: the unique tangent vector `v` at `ι x` such
that `⟪v, w⟫ = d(f ∘ ι⁻¹)(w)` for every tangent vector `w`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Mathlib `gradient` (`∇`, flat, whole-space fderiv) and `InnerProductSpace.toDual` (used inside the definition).
justification.name: YausConjectureOnTheFirstEigenvalue.tangentialGradient
justification.why_needed: Riemannian gradient of a function on M for the induced metric; Mathlib has no gradient on Riemannian manifolds.

blocks.name: tangentialGradient
blocks.text:
/-- The gradient at `ι x` of a function `f : M → ℝ` with respect to the metric induced by `ι`,
as a vector of the ambient space. It is the orthogonal projection onto the tangent space of the
ambient gradient of `f ∘ ι⁻¹` along `Set.range ι`: the unique tangent vector `v` at `ι x` such
that `⟪v, w⟫ = d(f ∘ ι⁻¹)(w)` for every tangent vector `w`. -/
noncomputable def tangentialGradient (f : M → ℝ) (x : M) : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (n + 2)) :=
  (ambientTangentSpace ι x).starProjection
    ((InnerProductSpace.toDual ℝ _).symm
      (fderivWithin ℝ (Function.extend ι f 0) (Set.range ι) (ι x)))

blocks.code:
noncomputable def tangentialDivergence (X : M → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (n + 2))) (x : M) : ℝ :=
  LinearMap.trace ℝ (ambientTangentSpace ι x)
    ((ambientTangentSpace ι x).orthogonalProjection ∘L
      fderivWithin ℝ (Function.extend ι X 0) (Set.range ι) (ι x) ∘L
        (ambientTangentSpace ι x).subtypeL)
blocks.docstring:
The divergence at `ι x` of a tangent vector field `X : M → ℝ^{n+2}` along `Set.range ι`,
with respect to the metric induced by `ι`: the trace over the tangent space at `ι x` of the map
`v ↦ P (D_v X)`, where `D_v X` is the derivative of `X ∘ ι⁻¹` along `Set.range ι` in the
tangent direction `v` and `P` is the orthogonal projection onto the tangent space. By the Gauss
formula, `v ↦ P (D_v X)` is the Levi-Civita covariant derivative of `X`, so this is the
Riemannian divergence.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Nothing in Mathlib; `LinearMap.trace` and `Submodule.orthogonalProjection` used as building blocks.
justification.name: YausConjectureOnTheFirstEigenvalue.tangentialDivergence
justification.why_needed: Riemannian divergence of a tangent vector field along the submanifold (trace of the Levi-Civita derivative P∘D); Mathlib has no connection or divergence on manifolds.

blocks.name: tangentialDivergence
blocks.text:
/-- The divergence at `ι x` of a tangent vector field `X : M → ℝ^{n+2}` along `Set.range ι`,
with respect to the metric induced by `ι`: the trace over the tangent space at `ι x` of the map
`v ↦ P (D_v X)`, where `D_v X` is the derivative of `X ∘ ι⁻¹` along `Set.range ι` in the
tangent direction `v` and `P` is the orthogonal projection onto the tangent space. By the Gauss
formula, `v ↦ P (D_v X)` is the Levi-Civita covariant derivative of `X`, so this is the
Riemannian divergence. -/
noncomputable def tangentialDivergence (X : M → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (n + 2))) (x : M) : ℝ :=
  LinearMap.trace ℝ (ambientTangentSpace ι x)
    ((ambientTangentSpace ι x).orthogonalProjection ∘L
      fderivWithin ℝ (Function.extend ι X 0) (Set.range ι) (ι x) ∘L
        (ambientTangentSpace ι x).subtypeL)

blocks.code:
noncomputable def laplaceBeltrami (f : M → ℝ) (x : M) : ℝ :=
  tangentialDivergence ι (tangentialGradient ι f) x
blocks.docstring:
The Laplace–Beltrami operator `Δ f = div (∇ f)` of the metric induced by `ι` on `M`,
evaluated at `x`. With this sign convention `-Δ` is a nonnegative operator.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Mathlib `laplacianWithin`/`Δ` in Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Laplacian (flat Laplacian on open subsets of inner product spaces, not on submanifolds).
justification.name: YausConjectureOnTheFirstEigenvalue.laplaceBeltrami
justification.why_needed: The Laplace–Beltrami operator of the induced metric (div ∘ grad); absent from Mathlib.

blocks.name: laplaceBeltrami
blocks.text:
/-- The Laplace–Beltrami operator `Δ f = div (∇ f)` of the metric induced by `ι` on `M`,
evaluated at `x`. With this sign convention `-Δ` is a nonnegative operator. -/
noncomputable def laplaceBeltrami (f : M → ℝ) (x : M) : ℝ :=
  tangentialDivergence ι (tangentialGradient ι f) x

blocks.code:
noncomputable def meanCurvatureVector (x : M) : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (n + 2)) :=
  ∑ k, laplaceBeltrami ι (fun y ↦ ι y k) x • EuclideanSpace.single k 1
blocks.docstring:
The mean curvature vector of `Set.range ι` in `ℝ^{n+2}` at `ι x`, namely the
Laplace–Beltrami operator applied to the position vector `ι` (componentwise). This equals the
trace of the second fundamental form of `Set.range ι ⊆ ℝ^{n+2}`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Nothing in Mathlib (no second fundamental form or curvature).
justification.name: YausConjectureOnTheFirstEigenvalue.meanCurvatureVector
justification.why_needed: Mean curvature vector of the submanifold in ℝ^{n+2} (Laplacian of the position vector = trace of the second fundamental form), needed to express minimality; absent from Mathlib.

blocks.name: meanCurvatureVector
blocks.text:
/-- The mean curvature vector of `Set.range ι` in `ℝ^{n+2}` at `ι x`, namely the
Laplace–Beltrami operator applied to the position vector `ι` (componentwise). This equals the
trace of the second fundamental form of `Set.range ι ⊆ ℝ^{n+2}`. -/
noncomputable def meanCurvatureVector (x : M) : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (n + 2)) :=
  ∑ k, laplaceBeltrami ι (fun y ↦ ι y k) x • EuclideanSpace.single k 1

blocks.code:
def IsMinimalInSphere : Prop :=
  ∀ x, meanCurvatureVector ι x ∈ ℝ ∙ ι x
blocks.docstring:
`Set.range ι ⊆ S^{n+1}` is a minimal submanifold of the unit sphere `S^{n+1}`: its mean
curvature vector in `S^{n+1}`, which is the component of the mean curvature vector in `ℝ^{n+2}`
tangent to the sphere, vanishes. Equivalently, at every point `p = ι x` the mean curvature
vector in `ℝ^{n+2}` is normal to the sphere, i.e. a multiple of `p` (by Takahashi's theorem it
is then equal to `-n • p`).

justification.name: YausConjectureOnTheFirstEigenvalue.IsMinimalInSphere
justification.why_needed: Predicate 'ι M is a minimal submanifold of the unit sphere': the mean curvature vector in ℝ^{n+2} is normal to the sphere, i.e. the mean curvature vector in S^{n+1} vanishes.

blocks.name: IsMinimalInSphere
blocks.text:
/-- `Set.range ι ⊆ S^{n+1}` is a minimal submanifold of the unit sphere `S^{n+1}`: its mean
curvature vector in `S^{n+1}`, which is the component of the mean curvature vector in `ℝ^{n+2}`
tangent to the sphere, vanishes. Equivalently, at every point `p = ι x` the mean curvature
vector in `ℝ^{n+2}` is normal to the sphere, i.e. a multiple of `p` (by Takahashi's theorem it
is then equal to `-n • p`). -/
def IsMinimalInSphere : Prop :=
  ∀ x, meanCurvatureVector ι x ∈ ℝ ∙ ι x

blocks.code:
def IsEigenvalue (μ : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ f : M → ℝ, ContMDiff (𝓡 n) 𝓘(ℝ) ∞ f ∧ f ≠ 0 ∧ ∀ x, -laplaceBeltrami ι f x = μ * f x
blocks.docstring:
`μ` is an eigenvalue of `-Δ`, where `Δ` is the Laplace–Beltrami operator of the metric
induced by `ι` on `M`: there is a smooth function `f ≠ 0` on `M` with `-Δ f = μ f`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `Module.End.HasEigenvalue` (would require packaging Δ as a linear endomorphism of a module of smooth functions; a direct predicate is simpler and more transparent).
justification.name: YausConjectureOnTheFirstEigenvalue.IsEigenvalue
justification.why_needed: Classical eigenvalue of −Δ with a smooth nonzero real eigenfunction, so that 'first eigenvalue is n' can be stated as `IsLeast` of the positive eigenvalues.

blocks.name: IsEigenvalue
blocks.text:
/-- `μ` is an eigenvalue of `-Δ`, where `Δ` is the Laplace–Beltrami operator of the metric
induced by `ι` on `M`: there is a smooth function `f ≠ 0` on `M` with `-Δ f = μ f`. -/
def IsEigenvalue (μ : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ f : M → ℝ, ContMDiff (𝓡 n) 𝓘(ℝ) ∞ f ∧ f ≠ 0 ∧ ∀ x, -laplaceBeltrami ι f x = μ * f x

blocks.code:
@[category research open, AMS 35 53 58]
theorem yaus_conjecture_on_the_first_eigenvalue {n : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) {M : Type*}
    [TopologicalSpace M] [ChartedSpace (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) M] [IsManifold (𝓡 n) ∞ M]
    [CompactSpace M] [Nonempty M]
    (ι : M → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (n + 2)))
    (hι : IsSmoothEmbedding (𝓡 n) 𝓘(ℝ, EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (n + 2))) ∞ ι)
    (hsphere : Set.range ι ⊆ Metric.sphere 0 1)
    (hmin : IsMinimalInSphere ι) :
    IsLeast {μ : ℝ | 0 < μ ∧ IsEigenvalue ι μ} n := by
  sorry
blocks.docstring:
**Yau's conjecture on the first eigenvalue** (Yau, 1982).
Let $n \geq 2$ and let $M^n$ be a closed (compact, without boundary) embedded minimal hypersurface
of the unit sphere $S^{n+1} \subseteq \mathbb{R}^{n+2}$. Then the first (nonzero) eigenvalue
$\lambda_1(M)$ of the Laplace–Beltrami operator $-\Delta$ of $M$ is equal to $n$, i.e. $n$ is the
least positive eigenvalue of $-\Delta$.

The hypersurface is given as a smooth embedding `ι` of a compact, nonempty, boundaryless smooth
`n`-manifold `M` into `ℝ^{n+2}` with image in the unit sphere. The restriction $n \geq 2$ excludes
the degenerate case $n = 0$ (a finite set of points has no positive eigenvalue) and the trivial
case $n = 1$ (closed embedded geodesics of $S^2$ are great circles, with $\lambda_1 = 1$).
The inequality $\lambda_1(M) \le n$ is known (Takahashi), so the open content is
$\lambda_1(M) \geq n$.
blocks.name: yaus_conjecture_on_the_first_eigenvalue

    (hι : IsSmoothEmbedding (𝓡 n) 𝓘(ℝ, EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (n + 2))) ∞ ι)

@[category API, AMS 53 58]
theorem tangentialGradient_const (c : ℝ) (x : M) :
    tangentialGradient ι (fun _ ↦ c) x = 0 := by
  have hc : ∀ y, Function.extend ι (fun _ ↦ c) 0 (ι y) = c := fun y ↦ by
    classical rw [Function.extend_def, dif_pos ⟨y, rfl⟩]
  have h : fderivWithin ℝ (Function.extend ι (fun _ ↦ c) 0) (Set.range ι) (ι x) = 0 := by
    rw [fderivWithin_congr (f := fun _ ↦ c) _ (hc x), fderivWithin_fun_const, Pi.zero_apply]
    rintro _ ⟨y, rfl⟩
    exact hc y
  simp [tangentialGradient, h]
blocks.docstring: The gradient of a constant function vanishes.
blocks.name: tangentialGradient_const

  have h : fderivWithin ℝ (Function.extend ι (fun _ ↦ c) 0) (Set.range ι) (ι x) = 0 := by
    rw [fderivWithin_congr (f := fun _ ↦ c) _ (hc x), fderivWithin_fun_const, Pi.zero_apply]
    rintro _ ⟨y, rfl⟩
    exact hc y
  simp [tangentialGradient, h]

@[category API, AMS 53 58]
theorem tangentialDivergence_zero (x : M) : tangentialDivergence ι 0 x = 0 := by
  have h : Function.extend ι (0 : M → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (n + 2))) 0 = fun _ ↦ 0 :=
    Function.extend_const ι 0
  simp [tangentialDivergence, h, fderivWithin_fun_const]
blocks.docstring: The divergence of the zero vector field vanishes.

theorem laplaceBeltrami_const (c : ℝ) (x : M) : laplaceBeltrami ι (fun _ ↦ c) x = 0 := by
  have h : tangentialGradient ι (fun _ ↦ c) = 0 := funext (tangentialGradient_const ι c)

claims.decomposer_note: Single universally quantified Prop: for every n ≥ 2 and every closed (compact, boundaryless — implicit in the list entry but explicit in the article and in Yau's original statement) embedded minimal hypersurface M^n of the unit sphere S^{n+1}(1), the first nonzero eigenvalue λ₁ of the (positive) Laplace–Beltrami operator −Δ on M equals n; the upper bound λ₁ ≤ n is known (Takahashi), so the open content is λ₁ ≥ n, and note Yau's original formulation quantifies over all closed (immersed) minimal hypersurfaces whereas the Wikipedia entry restricts to embedded ones — the statement's 'embedded' wording should be followed.
claims.reviewer_why: c02 is the only candidate that is correct as written with the simplest set of trusted facts: closed embedded hypersurface = Mathlib `IsSmoothEmbedding` of a compact nonempty boundaryless n-manifold into ℝ^{n+2} with image in the unit sphere; Laplace–Beltrami = div(grad) via tangential projections of `fderivWithin` along `range ι` (well defined since only values on the tangent space are used, unique by `HasFDerivWithinAt.unique_on`); minimality in S^{n+1} = mean curvature vector Δι(x) ∈ ℝ·ι(x) (classical; Takahashi gives Δι = −nι); eigenvalues = classical pointwise −Δf = μf for smooth f ≠ 0; conclusion `IsLeast {μ | 0 < μ ∧ IsEigenvalue ι μ} n` is exactly λ₁ = n. Boundary cases handled (`Nonempty M`, `2 ≤ n` per the decomposition notes). c04 is refutable for the empty manifold (IsLeast of an empty eigenvalue set). c03 and c07 are also faithful but rely on heavier machinery (pulled-back Hausdorff measure/weak formulation/local normal fields; sInf of Rayleigh quotients). My edits to c02: docstring explanation of the n ≥ 2 / nonempty restrictions, line rewrapping; Lean statements unchanged.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Yau's conjecture on the first eigenvalue

Yau's conjecture (1982) states that the first (nonzero) eigenvalue of the Laplace–Beltrami
operator on a closed embedded minimal hypersurface $M^n$ of the unit sphere $S^{n+1}$ is $n$.

Mathlib does not (yet) have the Laplace–Beltrami operator or the mean curvature of a Riemannian
submanifold. Since the hypersurfaces in question are submanifolds of the Euclidean space
$\mathbb{R}^{n+2}$, we define these notions extrinsically, from the ambient calculus:

* the tangent space of $M$ at $\iota(x)$ is the image of the differential of the embedding $\iota$;
* the gradient of a function on $M$ is the tangential projection of the ambient gradient, i.e.
  the unique tangent vector representing the differential of the function on the tangent space;
* the divergence of a tangent vector field $X$ along $M$ is the trace over the tangent space of
  $v \mapsto P(D_v X)$, where $P$ is the orthogonal projection onto the tangent space and
  $D_v X$ is the ambient derivative of $X$ along $M$ in the tangent direction $v$; this is the
  trace of the Levi-Civita covariant derivative of the induced metric;
* the Laplace–Beltrami operator is $\Delta f = \operatorname{div}(\nabla f)$;
* the mean curvature vector of $M$ in $\mathbb{R}^{n+2}$ is $\vec H = \Delta \iota$, the Laplacian
  of the position vector (equivalently, the trace of the second fundamental form);
* $M \subseteq S^{n+1}$ is minimal in $S^{n+1}$ if its mean curvature vector in $S^{n+1}$, which is
  the component of $\vec H$ tangent to the sphere, vanishes, i.e. $\vec H(p)$ is a multiple of $p$.

Derivatives along $M$ are taken with `fderivWithin` on the image of $\iota$; on tangent vectors
these are uniquely determined, and the definitions above depend only on their values on tangent
vectors.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Yau's conjecture on the first eigenvalue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yau%27s_conjecture_on_the_first_eigenvalue)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- S.-T. Yau, *Seminar on Differential Geometry*, Annals of Mathematics Studies 102, Princeton
  University Press, 1982, Problem Section.
- Z. Tang, W. Yan, *Isoparametric foliation and Yau conjecture on the first eigenvalue*,
  J. Differential Geom. 94 (2013), 521–540, [arXiv:1201.0666](https://arxiv.org/abs/1201.0666).
-/

open scoped Manifold ContDiff
open Manifold

namespace YausConjectureOnTheFirstEigenvalue

variable {n : ℕ} {M : Type*} [TopologicalSpace M] [ChartedSpace (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) M]
  (ι : M → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (n + 2)))

/-- The tangent space at `ι x` of the submanifold `Set.range ι` of `ℝ^{n+2}`, as a subspace of
the ambient Euclidean space: the image of the differential of `ι` at `x`. -/
noncomputable def ambientTangentSpace (x : M) : Submodule ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (n + 2))) :=
  LinearMap.range (mfderiv (𝓡 n) 𝓘(ℝ, EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (n + 2))) ι x).toLinearMap

/-- The gradient at `ι x` of a function `f : M → ℝ` with respect to the metric induced by `ι`,
as a vector of the ambient space. It is the orthogonal projection onto the tangent space of the
ambient gradient of `f ∘ ι⁻¹` along `Set.range ι`: the unique tangent vector `v` at `ι x` such
that `⟪v, w⟫ = d(f ∘ ι⁻¹)(w)` for every tangent vector `w`. -/
noncomputable def tangentialGradient (f : M → ℝ) (x : M) : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (n + 2)) :=
  (ambientTangentSpace ι x).starProjection
    ((InnerProductSpace.toDual ℝ _).symm
      (fderivWithin ℝ (Function.extend ι f 0) (Set.range ι) (ι x)))

/-- The divergence at `ι x` of a tangent vector field `X : M → ℝ^{n+2}` along `Set.range ι`,
with respect to the metric induced by `ι`: the trace over the tangent space at `ι x` of the map
`v ↦ P (D_v X)`, where `D_v X` is the derivative of `X ∘ ι⁻¹` along `Set.range ι` in the
tangent direction `v` and `P` is the orthogonal projection onto the tangent space. By the Gauss
formula, `v ↦ P (D_v X)` is the Levi-Civita covariant derivative of `X`, so this is the
Riemannian divergence. -/
noncomputable def tangentialDivergence (X : M → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (n + 2))) (x : M) : ℝ :=
  LinearMap.trace ℝ (ambientTangentSpace ι x)
    ((ambientTangentSpace ι x).orthogonalProjection ∘L
      fderivWithin ℝ (Function.extend ι X 0) (Set.range ι) (ι x) ∘L
        (ambientTangentSpace ι x).subtypeL)

/-- The Laplace–Beltrami operator `Δ f = div (∇ f)` of the metric induced by `ι` on `M`,
evaluated at `x`. With this sign convention `-Δ` is a nonnegative operator. -/
noncomputable def laplaceBeltrami (f : M → ℝ) (x : M) : ℝ :=
  tangentialDivergence ι (tangentialGradient ι f) x

/-- The mean curvature vector of `Set.range ι` in `ℝ^{n+2}` at `ι x`, namely the
Laplace–Beltrami operator applied to the position vector `ι` (componentwise). This equals the
trace of the second fundamental form of `Set.range ι ⊆ ℝ^{n+2}`. -/
noncomputable def meanCurvatureVector (x : M) : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (n + 2)) :=
  ∑ k, laplaceBeltrami ι (fun y ↦ ι y k) x • EuclideanSpace.single k 1

/-- `Set.range ι ⊆ S^{n+1}` is a minimal submanifold of the unit sphere `S^{n+1}`: its mean
curvature vector in `S^{n+1}`, which is the component of the mean curvature vector in `ℝ^{n+2}`
tangent to the sphere, vanishes. Equivalently, at every point `p = ι x` the mean curvature
vector in `ℝ^{n+2}` is normal to the sphere, i.e. a multiple of `p` (by Takahashi's theorem it
is then equal to `-n • p`). -/
def IsMinimalInSphere : Prop :=
  ∀ x, meanCurvatureVector ι x ∈ ℝ ∙ ι x

/-- `μ` is an eigenvalue of `-Δ`, where `Δ` is the Laplace–Beltrami operator of the metric
induced by `ι` on `M`: there is a smooth function `f ≠ 0` on `M` with `-Δ f = μ f`. -/
def IsEigenvalue (μ : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ f : M → ℝ, ContMDiff (𝓡 n) 𝓘(ℝ) ∞ f ∧ f ≠ 0 ∧ ∀ x, -laplaceBeltrami ι f x = μ * f x

/-- **Yau's conjecture on the first eigenvalue** (Yau, 1982).
Let $n \geq 2$ and let $M^n$ be a closed (compact, without boundary) embedded minimal hypersurface
of the unit sphere $S^{n+1} \subseteq \mathbb{R}^{n+2}$. Then the first (nonzero) eigenvalue
$\lambda_1(M)$ of the Laplace–Beltrami operator $-\Delta$ of $M$ is equal to $n$, i.e. $n$ is the
least positive eigenvalue of $-\Delta$.

The hypersurface is given as a smooth embedding `ι` of a compact, nonempty, boundaryless smooth
`n`-manifold `M` into `ℝ^{n+2}` with image in the unit sphere. The restriction $n \geq 2$ excludes
the degenerate case $n = 0$ (a finite set of points has no positive eigenvalue) and the trivial
case $n = 1$ (closed embedded geodesics of $S^2$ are great circles, with $\lambda_1 = 1$).
The inequality $\lambda_1(M) \le n$ is known (Takahashi), so the open content is
$\lambda_1(M) \geq n$. -/
@[category research open, AMS 35 53 58]
theorem yaus_conjecture_on_the_first_eigenvalue {n : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) {M : Type*}
    [TopologicalSpace M] [ChartedSpace (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) M] [IsManifold (𝓡 n) ∞ M]
    [CompactSpace M] [Nonempty M]
    (ι : M → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (n + 2)))
    (hι : IsSmoothEmbedding (𝓡 n) 𝓘(ℝ, EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (n + 2))) ∞ ι)
    (hsphere : Set.range ι ⊆ Metric.sphere 0 1)
    (hmin : IsMinimalInSphere ι) :
    IsLeast {μ : ℝ | 0 < μ ∧ IsEigenvalue ι μ} n := by
  sorry

/-- The gradient of a function is a tangent vector. -/
@[category API, AMS 53 58]
theorem tangentialGradient_mem (f : M → ℝ) (x : M) :
    tangentialGradient ι f x ∈ ambientTangentSpace ι x :=
  Submodule.starProjection_apply_mem _ _

/-- The gradient of a constant function vanishes. -/
@[category API, AMS 53 58]
theorem tangentialGradient_const (c : ℝ) (x : M) :
    tangentialGradient ι (fun _ ↦ c) x = 0 := by
  have hc : ∀ y, Function.extend ι (fun _ ↦ c) 0 (ι y) = c := fun y ↦ by
    classical rw [Function.extend_def, dif_pos ⟨y, rfl⟩]
  have h : fderivWithin ℝ (Function.extend ι (fun _ ↦ c) 0) (Set.range ι) (ι x) = 0 := by
    rw [fderivWithin_congr (f := fun _ ↦ c) _ (hc x), fderivWithin_fun_const, Pi.zero_apply]
    rintro _ ⟨y, rfl⟩
    exact hc y
  simp [tangentialGradient, h]

/-- The divergence of the zero vector field vanishes. -/
@[category API, AMS 53 58]
theorem tangentialDivergence_zero (x : M) : tangentialDivergence ι 0 x = 0 := by
  have h : Function.extend ι (0 : M → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (n + 2))) 0 = fun _ ↦ 0 :=
    Function.extend_const ι 0
  simp [tangentialDivergence, h, fderivWithin_fun_const]

/-- Constant functions are harmonic. -/
@[category API, AMS 53 58]
theorem laplaceBeltrami_const (c : ℝ) (x : M) : laplaceBeltrami ι (fun _ ↦ c) x = 0 := by
  have h : tangentialGradient ι (fun _ ↦ c) = 0 := funext (tangentialGradient_const ι c)
  rw [laplaceBeltrami, h, tangentialDivergence_zero]

/-- `0` is an eigenvalue of `-Δ` on a nonempty manifold, with the constant functions as
eigenfunctions. -/
@[category test, AMS 53 58]
theorem isEigenvalue_zero [Nonempty M] : IsEigenvalue ι 0 :=
  ⟨fun _ ↦ 1, contMDiff_const, fun h ↦ one_ne_zero (congrFun h (Classical.arbitrary M)),
    fun x ↦ by simp [laplaceBeltrami_const]⟩

end YausConjectureOnTheFirstEigenvalue

items: Extrinsic model: the hypersurface is `Set.range ι` for a smooth embedding `ι : M → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (n+2))` of an abstract compact smooth n-manifold; an embedded submanifold of ℝ^{n+2} contained in S^{n+1} is exactly an embedded hypersurface of S^{n+1}. 'Embedded' (Wikipedia wording) rather than Yau's 'immersed' is followed, via `IsSmoothEmbedding` (immersion + topological embedding).

Laplace–Beltrami operator defined as div(grad) for the induced metric using ambient calculus: tangent space = range of `mfderiv ι x`; grad f = orthogonal projection onto the tangent space of the Riesz representative of `fderivWithin ℝ (extend ι f 0) (range ι) (ι x)`; div X = trace over the tangent space of v ↦ P(D_v X) (Gauss formula: P∘D is the Levi-Civita derivative). Each `fderivWithin` is only used through its values on tangent vectors, where `HasFDerivWithinAt.unique_on` makes it canonical (tangent space ⊆ tangent cone), and smoothness of the relevant functions along the embedded submanifold guarantees differentiability within the image. Reviewer should check these two standard facts.

Minimality in S^{n+1}: the mean curvature vector of range ι in ℝ^{n+2} is taken to be Δ of the position vector (componentwise), a standard identity (Δx = trace of the second fundamental form); minimality in the sphere is that this vector is normal to the sphere, i.e. lies in ℝ ∙ ι x (equivalently, by the Gauss formula, the mean curvature vector in S^{n+1} vanishes; equivalently Takahashi's Δx = −n x).

'Closed' (explicit in the article and Yau's statement, implicit in the list entry) = `CompactSpace M` with boundaryless model `𝓡 n`; `Nonempty M` added because a hypersurface is nonempty and for the empty manifold the eigenvalue set is empty, which would make the statement false.

Hypothesis `2 ≤ n` follows the decomposition table notes. Without any bound the statement is false for n = 0 (no positive eigenvalues); n = 1 (closed geodesics of S², great circles, λ₁ = 1) is trivially true so excluding it does not change the open content.

'First eigenvalue is n' formalised as `IsLeast {μ | 0 < μ ∧ IsEigenvalue ι μ} n`, i.e. n is the least positive eigenvalue of −Δ; this includes the (known, Takahashi) fact that n is an eigenvalue. Eigenvalues are classical: a smooth (`ContMDiff … ∞`) real-valued f ≠ 0 with −Δf = μ f; by elliptic regularity this agrees with the spectral notion on a compact manifold.
Unit sphere: `Set.range ι ⊆ Metric.sphere 0 1` (radius 1 matters for the value n).

No connectedness hypothesis added (not in the statement; automatically true for closed embedded minimal hypersurfaces of the sphere by Frankel's theorem, and the least positive eigenvalue is well defined regardless).
Sign convention: Δ = div grad (nonpositive), eigenvalue equation −Δ f = μ f.

Bespoke definitions live in the problem file (the sandbox only allows writing candidate.lean); a maintainer may prefer to move the generic submanifold calculus to FormalConjecturesForMathlib. Basic API/test lemmas for the definitions are included with proofs (gradient is tangent, constants are harmonic, 0 is an eigenvalue on a nonempty manifold).

reviewer_notes: Ambiguities: the Wikipedia list entry has no dimension restriction; the decomposition table asks for n ≥ 2, which was followed (n = 0 would make the statement false — no positive eigenvalue on a 0-manifold; n = 1 is trivially true — great circles). 'Closed' (compact, boundaryless) is implicit in the list entry and explicit in the article/Yau; modeled as `CompactSpace M` with boundaryless model `𝓡 n`. 'Embedded' follows the Wikipedia wording (`IsSmoothEmbedding`), not Yau's immersed version. No connectedness hypothesis: the least-positive-eigenvalue formulation is meaningful regardless, and closed minimal hypersurfaces of S^{n+1} are connected by Frankel anyway. Candidate verdicts: c04 has a genuine bug — for an empty manifold N all hypotheses hold but `IsLeast {…} n` fails since `IsLaplaceEigenvalue ∅ μ` demands `∃ x ∈ ∅`; c03 and c07 are faithful but more intricate (c03: `Measure.comap` of Hausdorff measure — conditions do hold for a closed embedding with `BorelSpace`; weak formulation; universally quantified local unit normal fields; c07: `sInf` of the Rayleigh set, nonempty and bounded below so no junk). The bail-outs c01/c05/c06/c08 (missing primitives) are not persuasive: standard extrinsic submanifold calculus (tangential projection of ambient derivatives) expresses Laplace–Beltrami, mean curvature and minimality faithfully from existing Mathlib primitives, as c02 shows. Bespoke definitions live in the problem file (sandbox constraint); a maintainer may prefer to move the generic submanifold calculus to FormalConjecturesForMathlib. Standard facts a reviewer should confirm: (1) for a smooth embedding ι, tangentConeAt (range ι) (ι x) ⊇ range (mfderiv ι x), so fderivWithin is canonical on tangent vectors; (2) f ∘ ι⁻¹ is differentiable within range ι for smooth f (embedded-submanifold local extension); (3) Δι = trace of the second fundamental form, so Δι ∈ ℝ·ι characterises minimality in the sphere.
statement: Yau's conjecture on the first eigenvalue that the first eigenvalue for the Laplace–Beltrami operator on an embedded minimal hypersurface of $S^{n+1}$ is $n$.
